passkey-tpm 0.1.0-beta.3

> **Third beta — for testing, not daily use yet.** Please report problems with the [bug report form](https://github.com/dangerousplay/passkey-tpm/issues/new/choose) and include the output of `passkey-tpm info`.

passkey-tpm turns your laptop into a FIDO2 security key: passkeys live in the TPM 2.0 chip and are unlocked with your fingerprint (fprintd) or a PIN. It works with browsers, `fido2-token`, `pam_u2f` and `systemd-cryptenroll` through a virtual USB security key.

### Fixed in this beta

- **Firefox sign-in with a username** ([#5](https://github.com/dangerousplay/passkey-tpm/issues/5)): Firefox checks which passkeys the key holds with a silent request before signing in. passkey-tpm answered it with an error, so Firefox thought the passkey wasn't there. With a PIN it now gets a real answer that is marked "no user presence" and still needs the PIN.
- **The *Allow* question is no longer hidden** on machines without a fingerprint reader: the "Touch the fingerprint reader" notification is only shown when you have an enrolled finger, silent requests show nothing, and a prompt is closed as soon as its request ends.
- A silent request without a PIN no longer reveals whether a passkey exists for a site.

### What to test

- On a machine without a reader (or with no finger enrolled): register on [webauthn.io](https://webauthn.io) in Firefox, then sign in **with the username** and click *Allow*.
- The same in Chromium-based browsers, and with your fingerprint where you have one.
- Discoverable sign-in (no username), PIN changes from the tray, `hmac-secret`/PRF.
- Install, upgrade and removal of the package on your distribution.

### Packages

| File | For |
|---|---|
| `passkey-tpm_0.1.0-beta.3_amd64.deb` | Ubuntu 24.04+, Debian 13+ |
| `passkey-tpm_0.1.0-beta.3_amd64.rpm` | Fedora and other RPM distributions with `tpm2-tss` |
| `passkey-tpm_0.1.0-beta.3_amd64.pkg.tar.zst` | Arch Linux |
| `passkey-tpm-0.1.0-beta.3.tar.gz` | source tree layout (`cargo xtask dist`) |

Only x86_64 for now. Requirements: TPM 2.0 (`/dev/tpmrm0`), systemd, and fprintd for fingerprint use.

### Verifying the packages

Every package and `checksums.txt` is signed with [Sigstore](https://www.sigstore.dev/) by this repository's release workflow (`*.sigstore.json`), and GitHub keeps build provenance for each file:

```sh
cosign verify-blob --bundle passkey-tpm_0.1.0-beta.3_amd64.deb.sigstore.json \
  --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github.com/dangerousplay/passkey-tpm/\.github/workflows/release\.yml@refs/tags/v' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  passkey-tpm_0.1.0-beta.3_amd64.deb

gh attestation verify passkey-tpm_0.1.0-beta.3_amd64.deb --repo dangerousplay/passkey-tpm
```

### Known issues

- Any user in front of the screen can use `/dev/uhid`, which can create any kind of HID device, not only security keys. A dedicated helper is planned.
- `authenticatorReset` is accepted at any time, not only within 10 s of the device appearing.
- Wrong PINs are budgeted per user so one user can't lock the TPM for everyone; a correct PIN does not clear that budget before the TPM's recovery interval.
- Without a fingerprint, presence is a desktop notification: malware running as you that learned your PIN could click or fake it (especially on X11). A trusted on-screen prompt is planned.
- The tray and the presence notification were tested with automated tests, not yet on every desktop; please report how they behave on yours.
- Clicking the *Allow* notification's text (not its button) denies the request.
- The `.deb` uses Ubuntu 24.04 / Debian 13 library names and glibc 2.39 or newer.
